summary.text: Fermentation is anaerobic metabolism that breaks down organic molecules like glucose, passing their electrons to other organic molecules to make ATP.
It differs from cellular respiration, which passes electrons to oxygen or to other inorganic molecules.
It is inefficient, giving 2 to 5 ATP per glucose against 32 for aerobic respiration, yet humans have used it for 13,000 years to make and preserve food.

facts.label: Food use
facts.value: Humans have used it for 13,000 years

facts.label: Common products
facts.value: Lactate, acetate, ethanol, CO₂, succinate, H₂, propionate, butyrate

facts.label: In human muscle
facts.value: Supplies energy for 10 seconds to 2 minutes

items.prompt: A sprinter's muscles run short of oxygen mid-race. How can they still get energy for a little while?

options.label: Fermentation pathways add ATP briefly, until lactate builds up
They switch to a pathway that never tires
They burn fat with nitrate in place of oxygen indefinitely
They stop making ATP and run on stored heat

items.explain: Fermentation can augment aerobic energy for 10 seconds to 2 minutes in humans but is limited by the buildup of lactate.

items.prompt: Yeast in dough and a person breathing both break down sugar. Where do the electrons go in each?

options.label: Yeast hands them to oxygen; the person hands them to an organic molecule
Yeast hands them to another organic molecule; the person hands them to oxygen
Both pass them to oxygen, only at different speeds
Yeast releases them as heat; the person stores them as fat

items.explain: Fermentation transfers electrons to organic molecules, while cellular respiration transfers them to oxygen or other inorganic molecules.

items.prompt: A microbe lands where there is nothing to breathe. Why can it still make ATP by fermenting?

options.label: It borrows oxygen from the cells around it
It makes ATP faster than respiration, so oxygen is not missed
It runs on light instead of sugar
It needs no outside electron acceptor, so conditions do not stop it

items.explain: Because fermentation does not need an exogenous electron acceptor, it can occur regardless of environmental conditions.

items.prompt: A cell has one glucose and plenty of oxygen. Compared with using the oxygen, how would fermenting the glucose do?

options.label: It would yield about the same ATP
It would yield more ATP, since it is the simpler pathway
It would yield far fewer ATP, about 2 to 5 instead of 32
It would yield none, because fermentation makes no ATP

items.explain: Fermentation is relatively inefficient, producing 2 to 5 ATP per glucose versus 32 for aerobic respiration.

items.prompt: Why did people first start fermenting foods like dairy, grains and honey?

options.label: To make industrial chemicals like ethanol
Mainly as a way to preserve the food
To feed the microbes in their own guts
To give the food a longer list of ingredients

items.explain: Food as a substrate is the most common and oldest human use of fermentation, since it was a method to preserve food.

items.prompt: A cow's gut microbes ferment what it eats. What does the cow get in return?

options.label: Oxygen that the microbes release
Protein from digesting the microbes themselves
Nothing, since the microbes keep it all
End products it uses for energy

items.explain: Microbes in the gut release fermentation end products that humans and livestock then use for energy.
